function: Learned movable-antenna element positioning (MLP) with closed-form Rayleigh-quotient receive beamforming at the base station, maximizing SINR against multiple jammers (p. 1, p. 3).
system: Single-antenna source, base station with N-element linear movable antenna array (8 by default), K single-antenna jammers (3 by default); no RIS; frequency band not given (p. 2, p. 5).
method: Fully connected embedding and MLP (three fully connected layers, ReLU, Sigmoid output) mapping DoAs to antenna spacing ratios; unsupervised SGD training with loss 1/SINR (p. 4, p. 5).
data_channel: Field-response model with steering vectors of each transmitter's direction of arrival; source DoA randomly predefined, jammer angles uniform in [0, π]; 10^5 synthetic training samples (p. 2, p. 5).
test_conditions: Default setup 3 jammers, 8 antennas, region 7λ, dmin λ/2; Figs. 3-5 sweep antennas (3-8), region size (1-7λ), jammers (3-8); training per setting not stated (p. 4, p. 5).
baselines: Non-learned only: alternating optimization (AO) following [18], fixed-position antenna array with Rayleigh-quotient beamforming (FPV/FPA), random positioning and beamforming (RPB); no learned baseline (p. 5).
metrics: Achieved SINR versus number of antenna elements, normalized region size, and number of jammers; algorithm runtime in seconds versus antennas and jammers (p. 4, p. 5).
complexity: Order of complexity: training O(Ltr Lsp(Σ n_i n_{i+1} over embedding and MLP + N^3)), inference O(Σ n_i n_{i+1} + N^3); measured runtime in Fig. 6 (p. 4, p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "adopt the field-response based channel model, similar as [12], [18], [22]". A custom steering-vector model built from the directions of arrival; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 5: "There are 3 jammers, and the base station is with 8 movable antenna elements." Figs. 3-5 vary antennas, region size, and jammers, but the paper never says a network trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 5: "the following schemes are used as benchmarks": AO, FPV, and RPB, all non-learned. No earlier learned method or standard learned architecture is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "when the trained network is used for inference involving only single forward procedures, the complexity is" O(Σ n_i n_{i+1} + N^3); also p. 5: "Fig. 6. Algorithm runtime."
q5_support: p. 5: "The model is trained over a dataset with 10^5 samples" of random angles; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2410.20344v2 (4 Apr 2025) and carries no DOI; its title and authors give no sign of a different paper. Eligibility flag for the reviewer: Step 1.5 lists anti-jamming among the excluded functions, and the paper frames its goal as jamming mitigation (p. 1). I include it because the learned method solves max-SINR receive beamforming jointly with movable-antenna positioning at the base station (p. 2, problem (3); p. 3), that is the base-station beams of area 3, with the jammers acting as directional interferers; it learns no jamming detection, channel selection, or evasion decision. If anti-jamming is read as the function, the decision becomes exclude with reason function, p. 1. The MLP outputs the antenna positions, and the beamformer is the closed-form Rayleigh-quotient solution inside the trained pipeline (p. 3, p. 4); the positions are inferred per set of directions of arrival, so this is not antenna hardware design. Movable antennas are not a RIS (p. 1: "resembles reconfigurable intelligent surfaces"), so ris is 0. Single user only; the multi-user extension is discussed but not evaluated (p. 2, p. 4). q2: the network input (K+1 angles) and output (N-1 spacing ratios) change with K and N, and the paper does not say how the networks of Figs. 3-5 were trained. The FPV baseline of the text is labelled FPA in the figures. SINR in the figures appears linear (0 to 7).
